steps.heading: Start from the classical energy of a particle
steps.note: Kinetic plus potential. Nothing quantum yet — this is Newtonian bookkeeping.

steps.heading: de Broglie: matter carries a wave
steps.note: 1924. If light can behave as particles, particles can behave as waves.

steps.heading: Planck & Einstein: energy is quantised
steps.note: Energy relates to frequency, momentum to wavenumber.

steps.heading: Write a plane wave for a free particle
steps.note: The simplest wave carrying momentum ℏk and energy ℏω.

steps.heading: Differentiate in time — it pulls out the energy
steps.note: One time derivative returns E times the wave.

steps.heading: Differentiate twice in space — it pulls out p²
steps.note: Two spatial derivatives return p² times the wave.

steps.heading: Substitute both into the energy relation
steps.note: Replace E and p²/2m with the operators just derived.

steps.heading: The time-dependent Schrödinger equation
steps.note: Schrödinger, 1926. The Hamiltonian Ĥ generates time evolution.

steps.heading: Born rule: what the wavefunction means
steps.note: Born, 1926. Ψ is not observable — its squared magnitude is a probability density.

steps.heading: This is exactly what a quantum computer evolves
steps.note: A quantum gate is a unitary U — the solution of this equation for a chosen Ĥ.
